deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a calibration of the micrometer microscopes of the new Göttingen meridian circle. The microscopes are named 'unteres' (lower, L), 'rechts' (right, R) and an index (v). Thursday 30 April fits 1818, and the next page reduces star places to 1819. The previous page did the first half of a symmetric experiment: index on 0', lower microscope on 5'0". Readings were taken at circle positions 0°,15°,…,345°. It gave means L = 10"53 and R = 4'51"96.

(1) Second series ('Nachher folgende Ablesungen'). Index set on −5', microscope R on 0. For each starting position a ∈ {0°,15°,30°,45°,60°,75°}, readings (v, L) are taken at a, a+90°, a+180° and a+270°, giving 24 positions in all.

(2) 'Abstände': column means over the four quadrants.
- 0°: v = (8.7+7.8+6.5+7.4)/4 = 7.60; L = (17.95+19.0+18.1+16.8)/4 = 17.96.
- 15°: v = 33.2/4 = 8.30; L = 73.0/4 = 18.25.
- 30°: v = 8.30; L = 74.6/4 = 18.65.
- 45°: v = 32.0/4 = 8.00; L written 17.58, but the transcribed readings give 70.1/4 = 17.525.
- 60°: v = 33.1/4 = 8.275 ≈ 8.27; L = 73.3/4 = 18.325 ≈ 18.32.
- 75°: v = 8.30; L = 72.8/4 = 18.20.
- Grand means: v̄ = 48.77/6 = 8"13 and L̄ = 108.96/6 = 18"16.

(3) The line '−5'10"03 +8"13'. My reading: the measured interval for the lower microscope is −5' − (18.16 − 8.13) = −5'10"03, with the index/R part +8"13.
- First series: lower microscope interval = 5'0" + 10"53.
- Second series: 5'0" + 10"03.
- Difference 10.53 − 10.03 = 0"50. Hence Gauss's conclusion: the total run of the screw over one 5' division ('Inbegriff der Schraubengänge') of the lower microscope is 0"50 too large. He first wrote 'zu klein', struck it and wrote 'gross'.
- For R: 5'0" − 4'51"96 = 8"04 versus 8"13, a difference of 0"09. The stated 0"41 = 0.50 − 0.09 (my reconstruction, plausible but not certain).

(4) 'Mittlerer Ablesungsfehler' = √0.23013 = 0"480. A recomputation ('Nochmals') gives √0.1265 = 0"36. These are mean errors of a single reading in Gauss's sense, √(Σv²/(n−k)). The divisor and the residual set used are not recoverable with certainty. The listed 24 residuals give Σv² ≈ 8.47, i.e. ≈ 0.353 per value over 24, so the 0.23013 comes from a different residual set or divisor.

(5) Table of 24 values for 0°…345°, e.g. 0: −0.69, 180: +0.71, 345: −1.54. These are per-position residuals, apparently combining both series after removing the means. As on the previous page (where a fit −0"79 cos x + 0"03 sin x was used), they are roughly antisymmetric, f(x+180°) ≈ −f(x). That indicates a periodic (eccentricity/division) component. The exact combination producing these numbers could not be reconstructed.

(6) 30 April, 10h morning, level (Libelle) readings in three pairs. Means: (23.1+22.7)/2 = 22.9; (32.3+30.9)/2 = 31.6; (14.35+13.65)/2 = 14.0. 'Reducirt 3'21"94' is a reduced value that is not the plain mean (that would be 3'22"83). The reduction applied is not shown.
errors: 45° column, L mean: the transcribed readings 19.1, 16.8, 15.8, 18.4 average 17.525, but Gauss writes 17.58. Either one reading is misread (e.g. 15.8 vs 16.0) or there is a small slip. The effect on the grand mean is about 0.01" (18.15 vs 18.16).
The 0"41 for microscope R is not directly visible as a difference of numbers on the page; the reconstruction 0.50 − 0.09 is conjectural.
The Libelle 'Reducirt 3'21"94' differs from the arithmetic mean 3'22"83 of the three pair-means. This presumably reflects an unrecorded reduction, not necessarily an error.

results.what: Determination of the run (Run / total screw-turn value over one 5' division) of micrometer microscopes by reading the same division interval with two settings (index at 0 and at −5').
results.modern_name: Micrometer 'run' calibration of reading microscopes on a divided circle
results.usually_credited_to: Standard practice with Reichenbach/Repsold circles (Bessel, Struve, Gauss and others, c. 1810–1830)

results.what: Mean error of a single reading as the square root of a mean squared residual (√0.23013 = 0"48; √0.1265 = 0"36).
results.modern_name: Root-mean-square error / standard deviation of a single observation

results.what: Residuals around the circle showing a f(x+180°) ≈ −f(x) periodic pattern, modelled on the previous page by a·cos x + b·sin x.
results.modern_name: Harmonic (eccentricity) analysis of circle-reading / division errors
results.usually_credited_to: Routine astronomical instrument reduction (Bessel, Gauss, early 19th c.)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine instrument-calibration log for the Göttingen meridian circle: averaging, a micrometer run correction, and RMS reading errors. Gauss's use of mean errors and of such calibrations is well known. Nothing mathematically novel appears.

checkable.asserts: 45° column L mean is 17.525, not 17.58 as written
0.50" excess of the lower microscope's screw run
plain mean of level readings = 22.83", differing from the 'reduced' 21.94"

transcription_corrections: 0° row: v '8.7' and L '17.95' are overwritten corrections ('8"7' over another digit; '17.95' over '17.9').
In 'Der Inbegriff der Schraubengänge vom untern Mikroskop ist also 0"50 zu gross', 'klein' is struck and 'gross' added above. The second line reads 'Mikroskop Rechts 0"41 zu gross'.
Residual table, right column: the entry for 330 is written over another number (looks like '340' corrected to 330), value −0.60.
